I think all of these are harmless. Each name still points at the right element, so the search, the filter and the message box work as they should. Most of the warnings come from two flaws in Koda's own checks; one is a real slip in the app.

## How Koda looks up names
Inside a `ko-item`, an element answers to its `ko-as`, or else to both its `id` and its `name` (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/src/dom/names.js:58-83`). It then warns in two cases (`src/core/names.js:64-73`, reported at `src/dom/refs.js:526-533`):
- **"declared N times"**: the name was added more than once in the item.
- **"is not the #x on the page"**: the page also has an element with that `id`. Koda never checks whether it's the same element.

## Project landing page
`server/views/projects/page.eta:16` wraps the whole page in a `ko-item`. The designs list's `calc-ko-source` and `ko-invoke` (lines 79–80) name `q`, `stageReady` and `stageDesigning`:
- `<input id="q" name="q">` (line 70) gets added twice, once by its id and once by its name. That gives "declared 2 times", but both entries are the same input.
- `q`, `stageReady` and `stageDesigning` are found inside the item, and the page also has `#q`, `#stageReady` and `#stageDesigning`. Those are the same elements, so the "not the #… on the page" warnings are false.

Both are Koda flaws (0.1.4). The app markup is fine.

## Ask for fix page
- **"message" declared 2 times**: this one is real. In `server/views/_composer.eta`, the textarea in `_message-box.eta:7` declares `message` through `ko-as`. The hidden draft input at `_composer.eta:44`, `<input type="hidden" name="message" calc-value="message.value">`, has no `ko-as`, so its `name` declares `message` in the same item too. The textarea comes first, so it wins and the draft still copies the right value. But the clash is genuine.
- **"message" … not the #message**: the textarea has `id="message"`, and the label needs that id. It's the same element, so this is Koda's false positive again.

## The dropped `#app` answer
I agree, you can disregard it. `#app` on the project page (`page.eta:93`) reloads on `event:projects-changed` and `event:app-changed`. One of those events fired just as you clicked "Ask or fix…". The page was replaced before the answer came back, so Koda dropped it rather than attach it to an element that was gone. That's correct behaviour, just reported loudly. It would only be worth looking into if it happened on every visit, which would mean opening the fix page itself triggers one of those events.

## What I'd change
- **`server/views/_composer.eta:44`**: give the hidden draft input its own `ko-as` (e.g. `ko-as="draftMessage"`) so it stops declaring `message`. Leave `calc-value="message.value"` as it is.
- **Koda (`src/dom/names.js` `declarationsIn`, `src/core/names.js` `resolveName`)**:
  - Don't add an element a second time when its `id` and `name` match.
  - Only report "shadows" when the item's element isn't the element with that id.

  This is upstream: the change goes into Koda itself, not this project. Without it, the `q`/`stage*` warnings and the `#message` one will stay. The app could avoid them only by removing `ko-item` or ids that it needs.
Give me a prompt I can use on a Koda agent to fix it.

Here's a prompt you can paste into the Koda agent: ```text Two false warnings in Koda's name lookup inside a ko-item (seen in @kodalang/core 0.1.4). Repro:
Console shows: koda: "q" is declared 2 times in one ko-item - using the first koda: "q" inside this ko-item is not the #q on the page koda: "stageReady" inside this ko-item is not the #stageReady on the page Both are wrong. Each name resolves to the one element that also carries that id. 1. "declared N times" when an element's id and name are the same. src/dom/names.js, declarationsIn(): for an element without ko-as, it calls add(element.id) and add(element.getAttribute('name')). When the two are equal, the same element is added twice, so resolveName sees [el, el] and reports ambiguous: 2. Fix: never add the same element twice under one name. A name only counts as declared more than once when it's declared by different elements. 2. "is not the #x on the page" when the item's element is the page's #x. src/core/names.js, resolveName(): result.shadows is set whenever ids has the key, without checking the target. Fix: set shadows only when the winning target is not ids[key]. The warning is meant for a row whose `total` is a different element from the page's #total. Keep the real cases warning: - Two different elements in one item both declaring the name (e.g. a textarea with ko-as="message" and a hidden input with name="message") still report "declared 2 times". - An item element whose alias or name matches a different element's id elsewhere on the page still reports the shadow. Tests: add cases for both false positives (same element by id and name; alias, id or name resolving to the very element with that document id), and confirm the existing ambiguous/shadows tests still pass. Update docs/reference.md if it describes when these two warnings fire (codes name-declared-twice and name-shadows-id, reported from src/dom/refs.js). ``` Once that's released and Prelude picks up the new version, the `q`, `stageReady`, `stageDesigning` and `#message` warnings should go away. The duplicate `message` in `server/views/_composer.eta:44` is a real clash in Prelude's own markup, so this Koda fix won't remove it; it still needs the `ko-as` change on a branch here.
